fireworks/qwen3.8-27b.note: A dedicated deployment bills per GPU-hour, not per token, so no per-token price exists.

fireworks/qwen3.8-max.note: Fireworks bills cached input at the cached rate; a proxy that billed it at the full input rate overstated cost about 3x (LITELLMPRICE-01).

local/qwen3-coder-next-80b-a3b-6bit.note: Self-hosted: no per-token price. Hardware and power cost are not measured.

moonshot/kimi-k3.reference: Moonshot first-party published rate for Kimi K3

openai/gpt-6.1-sol.note: Short-context rate; long-context pricing above 272K prompt tokens is not modelled.

together/deepseek-v4.1-flash.note: Together discloses no cached-input rate, so cache reads are priced at the input rate.

zai/glm-5.2.note: Published rates, not yet reconciled against a Z.ai invoice. An earlier reading that Z.ai bills cache reads at the input rate was retracted (ZAIPRICE-02).

note: Per-token rates in USD per million tokens: input is fresh (uncached) input, cache is cache-read input, output includes reasoning tokens. Cache writes count as input at the input rate, so a provider's cache-write premium (Anthropic: 1.25x for 5-minute writes) is not included. A model absent from this table, or with source unknown, is priced unknown, never zero. Rates are what an API customer would pay; a run on a subscription plan is still priced at these API-equivalent rates. Proxy or gateway cost estimates are never a source.
